mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% q-o-q over last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% q-o-q.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 1% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by >1% y-o-y.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which negatively impacts earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three consecutive months of INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a broad-based demand shock, which depresses equity valuations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall >2% m-o-m
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST fall by >2% m-o-m.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month averages indicates a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above trend for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS above trend for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during four consecutive months of above-trend PAYEMS growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 5-year average, combined with a flat or declining personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), signals a savings glut that depresses demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 5-year average and GDPC1 flat or declining for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS exceeds its 5-year average and GDPC1 is flat or declining for three months.
